guide.summary: Forgejo documents an authorization-code OAuth2 provider where a registered app obtains a user token; OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token acts with the user's full access. Read-only listing uses the connected person's existing repository visibility, with pagination via page and limit parameters.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: Forgejo OAuth2 provider uses authorization code grant with PKCE; scopes are not implemented
findings.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider with the Authorization Code Grant plus PKCE, using authorize, access_token and userinfo endpoints. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, and tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user. Registration must be done on the instance's applications settings page.
findings.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts on their own Forgejo instances connecting through OAuth.

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.

findings.title: Register an OAuth2 application on the customer's instance and use its base URL
findings.detail: To use the Authorization Code Grant, the app must be registered in the user settings applications section; confidential or public client type must match the flow. The instance base URL is a user input for each customer instance.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer instance connection, before first test.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

findings.title: Authorization token is accepted as a Bearer token on the API
findings.detail: OAuth2 provider access tokens are accepted via Authorization Bearer header, consistent with the repository listing endpoints; the token acts as the consenting user.
findings.appliesWhen: Making API calls with the OAuth access token.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 Provider Access tokens obtained from Forgejo’s OAuth2 provider are accepted by these methods:
Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.

findings.title: Repository-scope permission read:repository covers listing repository routes
findings.detail: read:repository grants read access to repository operations under /repos/*. Documented applicable scope for read-only repository listing. Scoped tokens are a different mechanism from OAuth2, so this identifier applies only to access-token configuration and is recorded here as the least-privilege documented grant for repository reads.
findings.appliesWhen: Only if a scoped access token is used instead of OAuth; OAuth tokens are not scope-limited.

evidence.quote: read:repository Grants read access to repository operations, such as getting repository files, releases, and collaborators.
repository /repos/* API routes except /repos/issues/* : Repository file, pull-request, and release operations.
Repository and organization access

findings.title: Provider review and marketplace distribution policy not established in sources
findings.detail: The supplied sources do not document a provider review or marketplace listing process for third-party OAuth apps on customer instances.

evidence.quote: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

steps.title: Register OAuth2 application on the customer instance
steps.detail: The developer or customer admin registers a confidential OAuth2 application in the user settings applications page of the customer's Forgejo instance, with the app's redirect URI. Use the confidential client type for this first test path. The instance base URL is a user input (for example https://forgejo.example.org) and must be used for all endpoints.
steps.doneWhen: The app shows a Client ID and Client secret in Settings > Applications on the instance, and the redirect URI is recorded.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

fields: <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>: customer instance HTTPS origin, user-provided
CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET: from the app registration page

steps.title: Obtain user consent through the authorization endpoint
steps.detail: Redirect the connected person to the authorization endpoint on the instance. The user approves the app and is redirected to the registered redirect URI with a code and state. Check that the returned state matches the value sent. This is an unexecuted authorization step.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URI receives code and the matching state parameter after the user consents.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
CLIENT_ID: from registration
REDIRECT_URI: must match the registered redirect URI
STATE: random value generated by the developer app

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the returned code at the access token endpoint using the confidential client secret, grant_type authorization_code and the same redirect_uri. The response contains access_token used as a Bearer token. This exchange is an unexecuted authorization step.
steps.doneWhen: The response includes access_token, token_type bearer and refresh_token for later use.

steps.title: List first page of repositories visible to the connected person
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/repos/search with private=true so private repositories the connected user can access are included, with page=1 and limit=50. Send the OAuth access token as an Authorization Bearer header. The response is a JSON object, not a top-level array. Read each repository name from $.data[].name, where $.data is the array of search results in the response object, and join all names. Use --include to capture the Link and x-total-count headers. Boundary check: this is a read-only GET; do not call POST, PATCH or DELETE routes and confirm no repository is created, edited or deleted.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 is returned; names are read from every element of $.data[].name; the Link and x-total-count headers are captured for the next request.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
Response JSON paths for GET /api/v1/repos/search: $.data[].name (string)

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token exchange response access_token
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
private: literal true, to include private repositories the user can access
page: literal 1 for the first page
limit: 50, page size used in this request

steps.title: Request each following page using the Link header until none remains
steps.detail: Repeat the same read-only GET, using the next href exactly as returned in the Link header entry with rel="next", resolved against the instance host. Do not build or change a cursor. Read $.data[].name from each page and add it to the cumulative list. Continue following rel="next" links until a response has no rel="next" link, which is the documented end of pagination. Cross-check the cumulative count with x-total-count. Two pages alone are not a complete listing. Boundary check: confirm every request is a GET with the same token and that no repository is created, edited or deleted.
steps.doneWhen: Every page is read until a response has no rel="next" link and the cumulative name count matches x-total-count.

evidence.quote: returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.
< link: < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search ? limit = 1 &page = 2 > ; rel = "next", < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search? limit = 1 &page = 5252 > ; rel = "last"
... < x-total-count: 5252

fields: NEXT_PAGE_URL: literal href from the Link header rel="next" entry, unchanged
ACCESS_TOKEN: same access token

details.title: Forgejo OAuth2 provider uses authorization code grant with PKCE; scopes are not implemented
details.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider with the Authorization Code Grant plus PKCE, using authorize, access_token and userinfo endpoints. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, and tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user. Registration must be done on the instance's applications settings page.
details.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts on their own Forgejo instances connecting through OAuth.

preparation.title: Permissions rationale
preparation.text: read:repository: read:repository grants read access to repository operations under /repos/*. Documented applicable scope for read-only repository listing. Scoped tokens are a different mechanism from OAuth2, so this identifier applies only to access-token configuration and is recorded here as the least-privilege documented grant for repository reads.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register OAuth2 application on the customer instance
The developer or customer admin registers a confidential OAuth2 application in the user settings applications page of the customer's Forgejo instance, with the app's redirect URI. Use the confidential client type for this first test path. The instance base URL is a user input (for example https://forgejo.example.org) and must be used for all endpoints.
Fields: <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>: customer instance HTTPS origin, user-provided, CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET: from the app registration page

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Obtain user consent through the authorization endpoint
Done when: The redirect URI receives code and the matching state parameter after the user consents.

Exchange authorization code for an access token
Done when: The response includes access_token, token_type bearer and refresh_token for later use.

List first page of repositories visible to the connected person
Done when: HTTP 200 is returned; names are read from every element of $.data[].name; the Link and x-total-count headers are captured for the next request.

Request each following page using the Link header until none remains
Done when: Every page is read until a response has no rel="next" link and the cumulative name count matches x-total-count.
